Don't use flowery language and place the reader in first person/ Scenes might include solitary birthdays that morph into insights on self-reliance, quiet dinners that offer space for deep parental bonds, and the mature realization of the weight of carrying family expectations alone. A key question may be: In what ways does being an only child influence one's approach to life's challenges and relationships? response: As I sit here on my [birthday] alone, I'm struck by the realization that my solitary existence has taught me a valuable lesson about self-reliance. Growing up as an only child, I've had to navigate the world on my own, without the distraction of siblings or the comfort of shared responsibilities. (This has allowed me to develop a strong sense of independence, which has served me well in my [adult] life.) But it's also meant that I've had to carry the weight of family expectations alone, (which can be a crushing burden at times). I've often found myself wondering what it would be like to have a partner to share the load, or to have siblings to rely on in times of need. (Yet, as I've grown older, I've come to appreciate the quiet dinners I've shared with my [parents], where we've been able to connect on a deep level, without the distractions of others.) These moments have taught me the value of [parental] bonding, and the importance of nurturing those relationships, even when it feels like I'm shouldering the responsibility alone. (As I look back on my life, I realize that being an only child has given me a unique perspective on solitude, and has forced me to develop a strong sense of [self-sufficiency].)
